head: c49ebd030
summary: Every wall I attacked on tenant isolation, rank floors and replay held: viewer CLR04, cross-firm CLR11 with no existence oracle, clara_runtime 42501 on all three new doors, RLS reads firm-scoped, _reserve_op CLR10 on a reused key with different args, no regexp splice anchor anywhere in 0277/0278/0279, the firm-scope reviewed-barrier shas match the files byte for byte, and the lane's own 18 db cells re-run green after all the probing. Five defects are proved by running, two of them blocking. #932's policy outlives the enrolment shape it was validated against: ONE upsert_fa_account_profile with accum=null leaves a straight_line policy live, the next acquisition is born COMPLETE and unchargeable, and every depreciation run for that client then raises an untyped 23502 that no door can rescue. #975 enforces its own 'a judgement is made ABOUT an amount' law at record time but not at fold time: a fold_current recorded about 10,000 sen silently authorised folding 10,010,000 sen. Its refusal also states the client-wide arrears total as the named year's figure, and the remedy the refusal names refuses that very figure. reopen_prior is admitted on a year that is only 'closing', whose named remedy is not a lifecycle edge at all. And #932 shipped two new web door wrappers that mint crypto.randomUUID() inline, the exact D15 class #978, the last ticket in this same lane, exists to remove.

findings.title: A default policy outlives the enrolment shape it was validated against: the birth creates an unchargeable COMPLETE row and wedges the client's whole depreciation lane with an untyped 23502
findings.evidence: clara.set_fa_depreciation_policy walls this shape by hand (packages/db/migrations/0277_fa_default_depreciation_policy.sql:411-417, 'this account is a non-depreciable enrolment (no accumulated-depreciation account); its policy method must be none'). Nothing re-checks it afterwards: clara.upsert_fa_account_profile is pinned UNMOVED by 0277's own prestate, so re-issuing the enrolment with accum_depr_account_code = null leaves the straight_line policy row active, and the recut birth trigger (0277:546-556) copies v_pol.method / useful_life_months onto the register row while taking accum_code and expense_code from the NEW profile, i.e. NULL. DRIVEN on clara_l04 (scratchpad adv-l04-drift-min.mjs; ONE upsert, no explicit retire): setFaPolicy(straight_line/36) then upsertFaProfile({accumAccount: null, expenseAccount: null}) then buyAsset gives a register row {method:'straight_line', life:36, accum:null, expense:null}. clara.preview_depreciation_run then returns legs [{debit_cents:10000, account_code:null},{credit_cents:10000, account_code:null}], and clara.run_depreciation_manual raises SQLSTATE 23502 'null value in column "account_code" of relation "journal_lines" violates not-null constraint' -- not a typed CLR refusal. No door rescues it: clara.complete_fixed_asset_particulars refuses CLR37 fa_particulars_already_complete (the row IS complete) and clara.revise_fixed_asset_particulars(uuid,uuid,jsonb,date,text) refuses CLR37 'particulars carries an unknown key "depreciation_method"'. packages/runtime/lib/reconciler-fa.mjs isolates the throw per client (faFailed, faOk untouched), so the belt silently stops depreciating that client forever. Pre-0277 the shape was unreachable: the UNCOVERED branch (0277:558-566) births method 'none' whenever l.accum_code is null, and 0249's clara._fa_assert_particulars_completable refuses a hand completion of the same shape. This is a defect #932 introduced.
findings.required_fix: In clara._tf_fa_acquisition_birth (and the same lookup in clara._fa_on_approve arm 4), treat the account as UNCOVERED when the live profile carries no accum_depr_account_code and the live policy's method is not 'none': birth the pending row exactly as an account with no policy does. Add a cell that sets a depreciable policy, re-issues the enrolment as non-depreciable, acquires and asserts the run does NOT raise 23502.

findings.title: A fold_current judgement recorded about one amount silently authorises folding any later amount for the same year: RM 100 judged, RM 100,100 folded
findings.evidence: clara.record_fa_arrears_resolution enforces exactly this invariant at RECORD time (packages/db/migrations/0279_fa_closed_year_arrears.sql:359-372, CLR37 axis 'arrears_changed': 'the arrears for fiscal year % now stand at % sen, not the % sen this judgement was made about'), and its own comment (0279:305-310) says a judgement filed against a stale figure 'would put a stale ruling on the file'. clara._fa_run_period_core does NOT apply the same test at FOLD time: 0279:934-945 builds v_chosen from the CURRENTLY measured y->>'arrears_cents' and the STORED resolution's choice and id, and never compares the two. DRIVEN on clara_l04 (scratchpad adv-l04-stale.mjs): one closed year with arrears 10000 sen; recordResolution(choice='fold_current', arrearsCents=10000) stores arrears_cents = 10000; a second asset then placed in service INSIDE the same closed year lifts the year's arrears to 10,010,000 sen; clara.run_depreciation_manual PROCEEDS (status 'drafted', charged_cents 20,020,000) and its receipt reads arrears_folded[0] = {arrears_cents: 10010000, resolution_id: <the record whose own stored arrears_cents is 10000>}. Nobody was asked again. That is the IAS 8 basis the ticket names (a material prior-period error is restated; only an immaterial one is folded) defeated by a 1,001x drift in the very figure the materiality judgement was made about, and it is what the owner's ruling of 2026-09-20 calls 'a professional judgement Clara may not default'.
findings.required_fix: In clara._fa_run_period_core, treat a year whose live resolution's arrears_cents differs from the currently measured arrears_cents as UNRESOLVED: ask (manual) or park (swept) on a stated axis such as 'arrears_changed_since_judgement', naming both figures, so the accountant re-judges the amount that will actually move. AC2's 'a later run proceeds on the record without asking again' still holds for an unchanged figure, which is the case its own cell drives.

findings.title: The arrears refusal states the client-wide TOTAL as the named year's amount, and the remedy it names refuses that amount
findings.evidence: packages/db/migrations/0279_fa_closed_year_arrears.sql:884-900 raises with (v_arr->>'arrears_cents'), the sum over EVERY closing/closed year including years already answered fold_current, while naming only v_unresolved->0's label and id; detail.fiscal_years carries the per-year figures beside it. DRIVEN on clara_l04 (scratchpad adv-l04-multiyear.mjs) with two contiguous closed years, FY-A 10,000 sen and FY-B 20,000 sen: clara.run_depreciation_manual refuses with 'this run would charge 30000 sen belonging to fiscal year FY-A' (FY-A carries 10,000) and detail.arrears_cents = 30000 beside detail.fiscal_years = [{FY-A,10000},{FY-B,20000}]. Following the refusal's own remedy with the amount it stated, record_fa_arrears_resolution(FY-A, 'fold_current', 30000), is refused CLR37 'the arrears for fiscal year FY-A now stand at 10000 sen, not the 30000 sen this judgement was made about'. After FY-A is answered honestly at 10,000 the next refusal names FY-B and STILL says 30000, now including an amount already judged. The web surface escapes this only because apps/web/components/registers/fa-run-preview.tsx passes year.arrears_cents per year; the documented chat path does not. The #975 report's successor contract states that 'refusalSentence falls through to the door's own message VERBATIM, which is correct behaviour and already carries the amount, the year and both resolutions' -- false whenever more than one closed year carries arrears.
findings.required_fix: Raise and park with the NAMED year's own arrears_cents (v_unresolved->0->>'arrears_cents' / v_awaiting->0->>'arrears_cents') in both the sentence and detail.arrears_cents; if a client-wide total is wanted, give it a distinct key such as total_arrears_cents and never let a year-scoped sentence quote it. Same for the parked receipts at 0279:904-910 and 0279:926-931, which feed the belt log and the Work receipt. Add a two-closed-year cell: the existing battery only ever builds one.

findings.title: reopen_prior is admitted for a year that is only 'closing', and the remedy the park then names is not a lifecycle edge at all
findings.evidence: clara.record_fa_arrears_resolution admits any year with status in ('closing','closed') (packages/db/migrations/0279_fa_closed_year_arrears.sql:342-347), so 'reopen_prior' is accepted on a CLOSING year. clara._fa_run_period_core then refuses or parks on 'arrears_awaiting_reopen' with remedy 'reopen_fiscal_year' (0279:912-931). clara._tf_fiscal_years_lifecycle, read live off clara_l04, admits only open|reopened->closing, closing->open|closed and closed->reopened, so closing->reopened does not exist, and clara.reopen_fiscal_year is the closed->reopened verb. DRIVEN (scratchpad adv-l04-closing.mjs): FY-C at status 'closing' with arrears 10,000; recordResolution('reopen_prior') is ADMITTED; run_depreciation_manual refuses CLR38 arrears_awaiting_reopen with remedy 'reopen_fiscal_year'; the remedy's own write, update clara.fiscal_years set status='reopened', is refused CLR10 'fiscal year status closing -> reopened is not a lifecycle edge' (fy_lifecycle_edge_invalid). The client's depreciation is blocked and the stated escape cannot be performed; the only ways out are to supersede the judgement with the fold the accountant just rejected, or to finalise the close first -- neither of which the refusal says.
findings.required_fix: Either refuse 'reopen_prior' while the year is still 'closing', on a new axis naming 'finalise the close first', or make the park's remedy for a closing year say exactly that instead of pointing at clara.reopen_fiscal_year. Add a cell that records reopen_prior on a closing year and asserts the refusal names a reachable remedy.

findings.title: #932's two new web door wrappers mint the op key inline -- the exact D15 class #978 exists to remove -- and a retried set mints a second policy version
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/registers/fa-depreciation-policies.ts:78 and :95 both pass p_op_key: crypto.randomUUID() minted inside the wrapper, and apps/web/components/registers/fa-account-profiles-panel.tsx:173 and :272 call them with no key of their own -- there is no useDepreciationDecisionKey anywhere in that panel. #978's own report opens by calling this 'the one defect class #651 left out on purpose (named D15)' and fixes exactly the two pre-existing wrappers it names, while the two brand-new wrappers this same lane shipped three tickets earlier carry it. #975's wrapper does it correctly (recordFaArrearsResolution takes opKey; apps/web/components/registers/fa-depreciation-runs-panel.tsx:183,253 holds an arrearsDecision key), so the lane is internally inconsistent. Consequence DRIVEN on clara_l04 (scratchpad adv-l04-opkey.mjs): one human decision (straight_line/36) sent twice with two fresh keys -- the shape a retry after a lost response takes -- leaves TWO policy versions, v2 active and v1 retired 'superseded by set_fa_depreciation_policy v2'. A register row born between the two calls carries depreciation_policy_version 1 while the account reads v2, for one human act.
findings.required_fix: Give setFaDepreciationPolicy and retireFaDepreciationPolicy a required caller-supplied opKey plus an intent tuple matching clara.set_fa_depreciation_policy's own _reserve_op fingerprint (client, asset_account, method, useful_life_months, rate_bps, residual_cents -- 0277:361-364), and hold it on the profiles panel with useDepreciationDecisionKey, renewed when any field changes, exactly as #978 did for complete and dispose.

findings.title: The resolution record stores p_period_start / p_period_end verbatim with no validation
findings.evidence: packages/db/migrations/0279_fa_closed_year_arrears.sql:383-386 inserts p_period_start and p_period_end straight from the caller; nothing checks that they are the run's period, that they are ordered, or that they are in the past. DRIVEN (scratchpad adv-l04-walls.mjs): recordResolution(..., periodStart: '2099-01-01', periodEnd: '2099-12-31') is ADMITTED and stored. These columns are the ticket's own 'against that client, fiscal year and run' provenance, so a wrong pair makes the record read as a judgement about a run that never existed. No money moves on them, hence a note.
findings.required_fix: Either validate the pair (at minimum p_period_start <= p_period_end and p_period_end < clara._fa_today(), better against the client's cadence window), or state in the migration that these two columns are caller-asserted provenance only.

findings.title: In the frozen Work lane a parked run reads 'parked 0.00 across 0 charge row(s)' -- no amount, no year, no IAS 8
findings.evidence: packages/runtime/lib/depreciation-run.ts:269-276 (FROZEN, correctly untouched) maps any status other than posted/drafted to the raw status word and then prints charged_cents and entries, so a parked period renders as '<period>: parked 0.00 across 0 charge row(s).'. Its closedTail reads only still_due.skipped_closed, never the new still_due.closed_arrears, so a closed year carrying arrears with NO period skipped adds nothing at all. The #975 report names this as successor-contract item 3 and it cannot be fixed before the chatTurn_v22 / claraWork_v6 cut, so it is recorded rather than charged against the lane -- but until that cut a Work-lane reader is given a number (0.00) and a word (parked) that together read as 'nothing to do' for a run that is in fact waiting on a materiality judgement.
findings.required_fix: None in this lane. Carry it into the wave-4 shared cut as the successor contract already writes it, and make that cut's own cell assert the parked sentence names the amount, the year and the remedy.

held_up: Rank floors, DRIVEN on all three new doors (scratchpad adv-l04-walls.mjs): clara.set_fa_depreciation_policy, clara.retire_fa_depreciation_policy and clara.record_fa_arrears_resolution each refuse a firm-A VIEWER (carol) with CLR04 'insufficient role'.

Tenant isolation, DRIVEN: firm-B owner dave on a firm-A client, and firm-A bookkeeper bob on firm-B's client B1, both refuse CLR11 'client is not in your firm' -- the same code and the same message a non-existent client earns, so no existence oracle. clara.record_fa_arrears_resolution refuses another CLIENT's fiscal year with CLR37 axis 'not_this_client', the same refusal a non-existent year earns.

The machine role, DRIVEN: clara_runtime refuses all three doors with 42501 'permission denied for function ...', so materiality and policy really are human-only, as 0279 section B2 and 0277 section D claim.
RLS reads, DRIVEN: carol (firm A) sees firm A's 2 policy rows and dave (firm B) sees 0, on the same SELECT against clara.fa_account_depreciation_policies.

Replay, DRIVEN: the SAME op key with a DIFFERENT payload refuses CLR10 'op_key reused with different args' (clara._reserve_op, packages/db/migrations/0004_governed_fns.sql:56-58); the same key with the same payload replays the stored receipt and mints no second version.

Splice anchors: none to attack. 0277, 0278 and 0279 contain no regexp_replace or pg_get_functiondef splice; every recut body is a whole literal create or replace function, so the 'anchor matches twice or zero times' class does not apply to this lane.

The firm-scope gate waivers are honest: the two REVIEWED_DYNAMIC_SQL_BARRIERS entries added to apps/web/tests/firm-scope-db-pins.corpus.ts pin sha256 90656f46a5a89cc64e97938694c0e5139ab0d5eb6e8ab9cdeb8022a4cb380acb and ca9ede2bd4b065a8d3b4e67bde07b5afffbe937b2c1c083e580baf563de5a640, which are the measured sha256 of 0277 and 0279 exactly, and neither file (nor 0278) contains a 'create [or replace] view' of any spelling.

#978's key derivation is sound: disposeIntent's tuple is exactly clara.dispose_fixed_asset's own _reserve_op fingerprint, including cost_portion_cents and excluding p_memo (measured off the live prosrc), and completeIntent matches clara.complete_fixed_asset_particulars' (client, asset, particulars). There is no direction in which a legitimate retry earns CLR10, and none in which two different decisions share a key.

#975's cost in the belt's hot loop is not a regression on this rig: a client with six contiguous CLOSED fiscal years and nothing uncharged in them probes at 2.4 ms against 3.1 ms for a client with no fiscal year at all (8 probes each, scratchpad adv-l04-probe-cost.mjs) -- the v_after <= 0 short circuit at 0279:266-271 does what its comment claims.

The lane's own two new db batteries re-run green under the full 174-flag gate chain on clara_l04 after all of the probing above: tests/fa-depreciation-policy.test.mjs + tests/fa-arrears-resolution.test.mjs, 18 tests, 18 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.
not_covered: No concurrent two-connection race was driven against clara.set_fa_depreciation_policy or clara.record_fa_arrears_resolution. Both take pg_advisory_xact_lock(203005004, hashtext(client)) -- the SAME rung clara._fa_run_period_core and the particulars-completion doors take -- before touching their partial unique index, so the ordering argument is structural; it is asserted here from reading the bodies, not from a driven race.
clara._agent_depreciation_catchup_core was not driven (its close_prep wake source is registered-and-disabled); #975's own report names this and pins the body unmoved.
No from-scratch migration chain was run (the integrator's job); 0277, 0278 and 0279 were judged against the applied state of clara_l04 only.

Hosted data shapes were not exercised -- in particular a client with a long closed-year history AND uncharged months in several of those years, which is the state ADV-L04-3 reads worst in, and a real firm's fixed-asset register, which is where ADV-L04-1's wedge would first be met.
